argon_final.explanation: The 734.0 s audio recording contains a clean electrical hum signal, with a median frame quality of 22.81 dB, a valid frame fraction of 1.0, and strong median signal-to-noise ratios on harmonics 2, 3, 4, and 6 (193.02, 125.59, 280.63, and 183.63). Using the longest calibrated 600 s analysis window starting at 0 s across harmonics 2, 3, 4, and 6, the highest correlation against the 86350 s (24 h) 50 Hz reference trace is 0.78438 (with a second-best peak of 0.74538, margin of 0.039, and z-score of 3.07), which falls well below the required threshold of 0.87678. A second 600 s analysis window starting at 134 s using harmonics 2, 4, and 6 also failed to meet the 0.87678 threshold, reaching a peak correlation of 0.74851 (with a second-best peak of 0.73477, margin of 0.01375, and z-score of 2.95). Because the extracted frequency trace does not match the provided reference trace above the required threshold, the dating result is inconclusive.
argon_final.rationale: Two 600 s extractions covering the full 734.0 s audio recording (starting at 0 s with harmonics [2, 3, 4, 6] and starting at 134 s with harmonics [2, 4, 6]) both achieved valid_frame_fraction of 1.0 but produced low peak NCC values of 0.78438 (z-score 3.07, margin 0.039) and 0.74851 (z-score 2.95, margin 0.01375), well below the 600 s frozen threshold of 0.87678. Further configuration testing on shorter windows is unjustified and would only increase false-match risk, so we conclude INCONCLUSIVE using index 0 as the basis attempt.
